coordinates: pixels, x to the right, y DOWN. '_f0' columns = stabilised coords (frame 0 image, camera drift removed); '_raw' = position in that frame's own image. Camera drift is small (<= ~10 px during the ball flight), see camera.
description: Handheld-phone-style static shot of a wooden desk. A hand at the lower right holds a white ping-pong ball (Franklin logo), swings up and throws it to the LEFT at about frame 40. The ball bounces 12 times on the desk top, passing IN FRONT of (closer to the camera than) the red kettle, white cylinder, green glass bottle, juice bottle and white bowl, and leaves the image at the left edge (last partly visible frame 147). No other object moves.

camera.type: nearly static, slow drift (handheld or settling tripod)
camera.per_frame_file: tracks/camera_similarity.csv (scale, rotation, translation of frame i vs frame 0; p_frame_i = s*R*p_frame0 + t) and tracks/camera_shift.csv (phase-correlation shifts)
camera.drift_summary: translation vs frame 0: frame 41 ~(+1.5,+1) px, frame 100 ~(+4.5,-4.4), frame 147 ~(+9.5,-10), frame 216 ~(+11,-18); rotation <= 0.23 deg; scale 0.9985-1.0001 (no zoom)
camera.advice: Use the _f0 columns for motion (background-referenced). Differences raw vs f0 over the whole flight are <= ~10 px in x and y.

perspective.note: 2D scene by label, but it is a real 3D desk viewed roughly horizontally from slightly above. Motion is mainly right-to-left across the image (parallel to the image plane) with vertical bounces. The ball drifts slightly toward the camera as it goes left: table-contact image y of the ball centre rises from ~790 (first bounces) to ~810-819 (last bounces) and its apparent diameter grows from ~73-75 px (frames 50-90) to ~78-80 px (frames 110-140), i.e. ~6% scale change. Annotators used a single planar scale.

objects.name: ball
objects.distinguish: small white sphere with black 'Franklin' logo; the only moving object besides the hand
objects.visible_frames: 0-147 (0-36 held in hand, partly covered by fingers; 37-40 in the throwing hand, blurred; 41-147 free flight / bouncing; 140-147 cut by the left image edge; 148-216 out of frame)
objects.reference_point: visible centre of the ball (centroid of white segmented blob; arc-fit fill where the ball is low-contrast against the white bowl/cylinder)

apparent_diameter_px.note: Horizontal width is inflated by horizontal motion blur (+2..8 px), vertical height by vertical blur near bounces (up to +30 px). Use the minor axis (mask_minor_px) at apex frames for the diameter.

objects.track: tracks/hand.csv (rough skin-colour bbox; frames 0-36 bbox includes the ball; 46-62 bbox is mostly the shadow)
